_doc: Manners: each faction's personality, read from the data it already has, never written per faction. A people's come from its history.json lineage traits, its might and how warm it starts, plus its ruler's temperament (neighbours.json temperaments); a power's from its powers.json likes and evil; a menace's from its lineage ambitions plus its kind's temper this campaign. Each manner moves the DCs of the skills it answers to (dc: negative is easier), lends one option to a first meeting (greet, then terms), one to an enemy herald's visit (parley) and one ongoing overture in the Diplomacy window. First meetings are composed from these at load (Systems/Manners.cs): contact-people-<people id>, contact-menace-<lineage>, contact-signs-<lineage>. Arrivals are the opening line per people (by its id, for peoples that share a lineage) or per lineage; a lineage without one gets the role's fallback with its first manner's arrive clause. In greet/terms/parley effects, warm is what they think of the town (regard for a people, minor for a power).

fallback.people: Riders from {settlement} come to the gate: {people}, sent by {leader}. They come {arrive}.
fallback.menace: A herald of {menace} comes to the gate with words from {foeLeader}. They come {arrive}.
fallback.signs: Signs of {menace} near {town}: tracks, carcasses, and quiet where there should be birds.

terms: Before they go, {leader}'s envoy speaks plainly. {motive}

arrivals.cloud-court: A cloud castle's shadow crosses the fields at noon. A giant herald of {settlement} comes down a rope of mist to ask what {town} offers the court above.
arrivals.griffon-clans: Three griffons wheel over the walls and land on the green. A rider of {settlement} asks who rules here, and whether {town} keeps meat for their mounts.
arrivals.gold-ancient: A gold dragon circles the town once, then sets down outside the gate. In a clear, patient voice it asks after {town}'s laws and who keeps them.
arrivals.silver-ancient: An old traveller in grey walks in from the hills and leaves a silver scale on the inn table. {leader} of {settlement} would know {town}'s heart.
arrivals.bronze-ancient: Thunder rolls out of a clear sky over the harbour road. A bronze dragon lands by the well and asks who in {town} would stand against the sea's raiders.
arrivals.brass-ancient: A brass dragon lands in the market square, sends the stalls flying, and asks loudly for the best talker in {town}. It has all afternoon.
arrivals.copper-ancient: A copper dragon perches on the town hall roof and asks the crowd a riddle. Whoever answers may hear what {leader} of {settlement} wants of {town}.
arrivals.river-folk: A cart comes up the river road from {settlement}, heaped with cheese and turnips. {leader} walks beside it, cap in hand, to meet the new neighbours.
arrivals.march-halflings: Three ponies and far more halflings than should fit on them arrive from {settlement}, with a basket for whoever opens the gate. {leader} has sent pie.
arrivals.deep-realm: Dwarves of {settlement} march to the gate in step, beards braided. {leader}'s herald asks, flatly, whether {town} knows a dragon when it sees one.
arrivals.first-leaves: Nobody sees them come. At dawn there are elves of {settlement} under the oak by the gate, watching the woodcutters. {leader} waits to be noticed.
arrivals.deep-gnomes: A gnome of {settlement} climbs out of a well in the market, unrolls a map of everything under {town}, and asks who is in charge of buying it.
arrivals.fen-folk: Lizardfolk of {settlement} stand at the edge of the fields at dawn, very still, holding eels. {leader} has sent them to taste the air of the new town.
arrivals.dawn-templars: Brothers and sisters of {settlement} ride in under the dawn banner. Before anything else they ask where {town} buries its dead, and how deep.
arrivals.free-port-folk: A captain of {settlement} arrives with a clerk, a lawyer and a crate of wine, and asks what {town} charges in harbour dues. There is no harbour. She asks anyway.
arrivals.tidekin: At low tide there are tidekin of {settlement} on the rocks below the town, singing softly, leaving pearls in a shell for whoever climbs down.
arrivals.isle-city: A tall ship of {settlement} drops anchor where everyone can see it. Its purser comes ashore to count what {town} has worth buying, and what it ought to pay.
arrivals.frost-jarls: Frost-sworn of {settlement} ride in wrapped in wolf fur and lay an axe across the council table. {leader} wants to know if {town} is worth the walk.
arrivals.sunpaw-clans: A sunpaw scout of {settlement} is found asleep in the council chamber, having read every letter on the desk. She would like to talk terms. And cream.
arrivals.kestrine-eyries: A kestrine of {settlement} lands on the bell tower and will not come down. It shouts that {leader} would hear what the new town wants with the high places.
arrivals.hollow-legion: Empty armour of {settlement} marches to the gate, stops, and waits. A voice from inside the helm asks whether {town} serves the rightful king.
arrivals.oasis-heirs: A caravan of {settlement} kneels its camels outside the gate. {leader}'s steward unrolls a carpet, pours date wine, and asks nothing at all for an hour.
arrivals.red-tide: A rider in a red-daubed helm flings a broken standard at the gate: {foeLeader} sends greetings, and asks how many fighters {town} has.
arrivals.warren-clans: A goblin herald with a white rag on a stick pops out of a drain. {foeLeader}, it squeaks, would discuss terms. And the pantry.
arrivals.stoneking-giants: The ground shakes before the herald comes: a giant of {menace} with a cart for a satchel. {foeLeader} wants to know who built a town on the Stonekings' road.
arrivals.rime-giants: Frost creeps over the gate at noon. A giant of {menace} stands beyond it, breath like a blizzard, with words from {foeLeader}.
arrivals.hollow-court: At midnight a herald knocks at the gate, pale as linen and smelling of the grave. {foeLeader} invites {town} to dine.
arrivals.ninefold-dead: A gilded scribe of the dead arrives on a bier and reads out a writ: {town} stands on land of the Ninefold Throne, and owes it nine hundred years of rent.
arrivals.drowned: A drowned man walks out of the river, water pouring from his mouth as he speaks the words of {foeLeader}.
arrivals.last-door: A gift arrives with no giver: a silver mirror. When the mayor looks in it, {foeLeader} looks back, and smiles.
arrivals.broken-pact: A fey herald steps out of a ring of mushrooms that was not there yesterday, bows too low, and recites terms nobody asked for, from {foeLeader}.
arrivals.coil-whisperers: A snake in the council chamber speaks in a woman's voice: {foeLeader} would be friends with {town}. For now.
arrivals.tyranny-broods: Livestock gone, sheds clawed open, a scale the size of a shield in the mud: {menace} has found {town}'s scent.
arrivals.wyrm-blood: A dragonborn herald in red lacquer lands a wyvern in the market and demands whoever owns the gold here, on behalf of {foeLeader}.
arrivals.ash-regents: Ash falls on {town} for an hour. Then a kobold herald in a crown too big for it arrives to read {foeLeader}'s terms.
arrivals.elder-wild: The trees lean toward {town} overnight. Something in the deep wood has noticed the axes: {menace}.
arrivals.marcher-pretender: A herald in quartered colours trumpets at the gate: {foeLeader}, rightful lord of these marches, will hear {town}'s oath of fealty now.
arrivals.corsairs: A corsair longboat beaches below the town. Its captain tosses a purse to the watch: {foeLeader} pays well for friends, and better for silence.
arrivals.caravan-princes: A prince's factor arrives with a ledger and armed men, and asks {town} to sign a small contract with {menace}. A very small one.
arrivals.hollow-choir: Singing in the streets at night: three townsfolk in grey, eyes shut, singing the hymn of {menace}. None of them remember it in the morning.
arrivals.last-door-fiends: A smell of sulphur, a scorch mark on the council table, and a contract in red ink, already signed by {foeLeader}.
arrivals.gnoll-packs: Laughter in the hills all night. At dawn a gnoll of {menace} stands on the ridge holding up a sheep's head, and laughs again for {foeLeader}.
arrivals.ember-kennel: Scorched paw prints the size of plates circle the town, and the dogs won't stop howling: {menace} hunts here now.
arrivals.spirit-callers: The dead of {town}'s graveyard are seen at dusk, walking back to their old homes. A voice on the wind says {foeLeader} would speak with the living.
arrivals.black-bough: An arrow fletched with black leaves pins a letter to the gate: {foeLeader} claims the forest, and every road in it.
arrivals.forge-giants: A wheel of red-hot iron rolls to the gate and stops. Behind it comes a giant of {menace} with a hammer like a tower, and a message from {foeLeader}.
arrivals.cloud-lords: A shadow passes over {town} at noon: a castle on a cloud. A rope ladder drops into the square, and a herald climbs down to announce {foeLeader}.
arrivals.storm-kings: Lightning strikes the bell tower three times, and a voice in the thunder names {foeLeader}, king of the storm.

success.text: They see a town that guards its gate, and respect it, a little.

failure.text: They leave muttering. {leader} will hear that the new town is rude.

success.text: {town} keeps its counsel, and they go home.

dismiss.label: Send the herald back with nothing

success.text: The herald goes as it came. {menace} will make of that what it likes.

people.text: Nobody comes to the gate. They wait a day, then turn for home.

menace.text: Nobody answers. The herald leaves its words nailed to the gate, and they frighten people.

signs.text: Nobody looks into it, and the stories grow in the telling.

success.text: The trail runs straight back to its lair. Now {town} knows where it sleeps.

failure.text: The trail goes cold in the rocks.

success.text: Bells, salt and bonfires on the roads. People sleep easier.

failure.text: Something knocks the bonfires over in the night.

signs.label: Burn the carcasses and say nothing

success.text: The smoke drifts over the walls, and the talk dies down, mostly.

manners.name: Proud
manners.tip: Honour matters more than gold · threats backfire
manners.arrive: under their banners, and wait to be greeted first

success.text: They straighten at the old titles. Someone in {town} knows who they are.

failure.text: You stumble over a title, and the silence is long.

terms.label: Promise them a place of honour at your table

success.text: They will be seated first at every feast in {town}. They like that very much.

parley.label: Receive the herald with full ceremony

success.text: Flattered, the herald boasts of its master's halls, and lets slip where they are.

failure.text: The herald takes the ceremony as fear.

overture.name: Sing their deeds
overture.won: The town crier tells the old victories of {name} in the square. Word reaches them.
overture.lost: The crier gets the old battle wrong, and {name} hear of it.

manners.name: Greedy
manners.tip: Everything has a price · gold speaks loudest
manners.arrive: with scales and a clerk, ready to buy or sell

success.text: You agree on prices that suit you both, and they buy a little on the spot.

failure.text: They name a price that insults you both.

terms.label: Offer first pick of the market

success.text: You guess what they are short of. They buy it at once, and gladly.

failure.text: You misjudge what they need, and nothing changes hands.

parley.label: Pay the herald to carry a gift home

success.text: Gold is understood everywhere. {menace} is in no hurry now.

overture.name: Send a purse
overture.won: The purse is counted twice and found pleasing. {name} think better of {town}.
overture.lost: {name} take the purse and grumble that it was light.

manners.name: Shy
manners.tip: Keep your distance · no tricks, no pressure
manners.arrive: quietly, and keep to the edge of the fields

greet.label: Let them come in their own time

success.text: You leave the gate open and send nobody out. By evening they come in, quietly, and seem grateful.

terms.label: Promise to keep your riders off their land

success.text: They want nothing more than that. They will hold you to it.
Your tracker comes back with the way to its master's lair.

failure.text: Your tracker comes back with nothing, and a cut on the cheek.

overture.name: Leave them in peace
overture.won: No envoys, no riders: only a gift left at the boundary stone. {name} take it, and are glad of the quiet.

manners.name: Generous
manners.tip: Glad to share · ask, and be grateful
manners.arrive: with full baskets, as if to a neighbour

success.text: The baskets go round the square. {town} eats well tonight, and they are pleased to see it.

terms.label: Promise to share in lean years

success.text: They clasp hands on it. Neither side will go hungry while the other eats.

failure.text: The promise sounds hollow, even to you.

parley.label: Send the herald off with bread

success.text: The herald eats, and talks, and some of its anger goes out of it.

failure.text: The herald throws the bread in the ditch.

overture.name: Ask a kindness
overture.won: {name} send carts of food, and are glad to be asked.
overture.lost: {name} have little to spare this season, and say so.

manners.name: Gregarious
manners.tip: Love company · feasts and fairs win them
manners.arrive: singing, more of them than were sent

success.text: They eat well and sing louder. {leader} will hear the new town keeps a good table.

terms.label: Invite them to the next fair

success.text: They promise to come, and bring friends. The fair will be loud.
By the third jug the herald is telling you where its master sleeps.

failure.text: The herald drinks you under the table and leaves laughing.

overture.name: Host a feast
overture.won: {name} come to {town} for a feast and stay for three days. Everyone is sorry to see them go.
overture.lost: The feast is dull and the ale is thin. {name} go home early.

manners.name: Fierce
manners.tip: Respect strength · meet a challenge, never dodge it
manners.arrive: armed, and looking for a fight to judge you by

success.text: You win the wrestling bout by a hair. They roar and pound the table. A town with a spine.

failure.text: You end up in the horse trough. They laugh a long time.

terms.label: Swear to stand with them in battle

success.text: They cut their palms and yours. It is a serious oath to them.
You meet the herald's stare until it looks away. The town cheers.

failure.text: Your voice cracks. The herald laughs, and so does the story of it.

overture.name: Champion's bout
overture.won: {town}'s champion throws {name}'s best into the dust. They have not had such a good day in years.
overture.lost: {town}'s champion is carried off the field. {name} make songs about it.

manners.name: Romantic
manners.tip: Moved by songs and grand gestures
manners.arrive: garlanded, with a poet to remember the day

success.text: Your song makes their poet weep. That counts for a great deal.

failure.text: You forget the second verse. Politely, they sing it for you.

terms.label: Name a street after their heroes

success.text: A new sign goes up by the square, and their poet writes it into a song.
The herald cannot resist a rhyme, and rhymes its master's lair with 'despair'.

failure.text: The herald's verse is better than yours, and crueller.

overture.name: Send a bard
overture.won: {town}'s bard sings for {name} under the stars. They will remember the night.
overture.lost: The bard's voice fails in the cold. {name} are kind about it, which is worse.

manners.name: Ambitious
manners.tip: Want to rise · back their plans and share the gains
manners.arrive: with plans already drawn, to see what use you are

greet.label: Talk of what you could build together

success.text: Their eyes light up at roads and markets that don't exist yet. They want in.

failure.text: Your plans sound small to them.

terms.label: Promise them a share of the roads

success.text: A share of every caravan's tolls, in writing. They sign quickly.

failure.text: They want a bigger share than you can give.

success.text: You listen well. Its master wants more than {town}, and the herald says where it rules from.

failure.text: The offer is a trap, and you nearly walk into it.

overture.name: Back their claim
overture.won: {town}'s gold and letters back {name}'s plans. They prosper, and know whom to thank.
overture.lost: {name} take the gold, but say {town} backed them too timidly.

manners.name: Pious
manners.tip: Faith first · share the rites, never mock them
manners.arrive: behind a priest, with a blessing for the gate

success.text: You know the words of their prayer. They are moved that a stranger does.

failure.text: You kneel at the wrong moment.

terms.label: Promise a shrine to their faith

success.text: A small shrine goes up by the gate. Their pilgrims will stop there.
The herald will not cross the blessed line, and the town sees it.

failure.text: The herald steps over the line and smiles.

overture.name: Share the rites
overture.won: {town}'s priests keep a holy day with {name}. Their shrines feel safer for it.
overture.lost: The rites go wrong in small ways that {name} notice.

manners.name: Cunning
manners.tip: Every word weighed · lies are seen through

success.text: You answer every probing question with a better one. They are impressed, and a little wary.

failure.text: They learn far more about {town} than you learn about them.

success.text: Letters, ciphers and the odd useful rumour, both ways. They like the arrangement.

failure.text: Your first letter is read by the wrong people.

success.text: The herald goes home with a picture of a town that doesn't exist. Its master will plan for the wrong one.

failure.text: The herald sees through you, and its master will remember the insult.

overture.name: Trade secrets
overture.won: {name} trade a secret for a secret, and tell {town} of a place near them worth knowing.
overture.lost: {name} got the better of the trade, and they know it.

manners.name: Cruel
manners.tip: Respect only fear · kindness looks like weakness
manners.arrive: with something dead tied to the lead horse

success.text: You don't flinch. They decide {town} is worth dealing with.

failure.text: They smell fear on you, and enjoy it.

success.text: They take the gold without thanks. It buys peace, for now.
The herald looks at the rope a long time, then leaves faster than it came.

failure.text: The herald laughs at the gallows: it has seen far worse, and done it.

overture.name: Pay their price
overture.won: {town} pays what {name} ask. They are pleased. The townsfolk are not.

manners.name: Timid
manners.tip: Easily frightened · reassure them, offer shelter
manners.arrive: few, and nervous, ready to run

success.text: They stop glancing at the road behind them, and stay for supper.

failure.text: Something you say frightens them, and they leave early.

terms.label: Promise your walls if trouble comes

success.text: Shelter behind {town}'s walls: it is the thing they wanted most.

parley.label: Call the watch out in force

success.text: Every spear in {town} lines the gate. The herald turns pale and goes.

failure.text: The watch turns out late and ragged.

overture.name: Offer protection
overture.won: {town}'s watch rides {name}'s roads for a week. They feel safer, and thank you for it.
overture.lost: {name} hear the offer as a threat.
